chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him), who said:
He (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I have not eaten a foodstuff which is more remaining nor more stirring for the illnesses than the dried meat, meaning the Jerk'.

key_terms.الْقَدِيدَ: jerk / dried meat (specifically salted and dried beef)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the health effects of dried meat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies dried meat (qadeed) as the most lingering food in the stomach and the most likely to provoke illness, reflecting the Shia medical tradition's emphasis on digestion and dietary moderation. This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the practical wisdom of avoiding heavy, preserved meats to maintain bodily health and spiritual clarity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Isa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3rd, said, ‘
He<sup>asws</sup> used to say: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have not eaten a foodstuff which is more remaining nor more stirring for the illnesses than the dried meat, meaning the Jerk’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Musa ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Thalith, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
would say, ‘I have not used anything for food more inducing illnesses than dried up meat, that is, al-Qadid.’”
